## Resources

### Readings

1.   Cheat sheet and other documentation for [purrr package](https://purrr.tidyverse.org/)
2.   (optional) For a deeper discussion of purrr vs. for loops read  [R for Data Science Chapter 21](https://r4ds.had.co.nz/iteration.html). Section 21.5 focuses on the `map()` if you want a quick summary/review of that function.
3.   [The Book of Mormon](https://www.lds.org/scriptures/bofm?lang=eng). This link is for reference only. You don't have to read the full BOM before completing this assignment.

### Guided Instruction

Review/complete the guided instruction for the other tasks in this module if you have not yet.

## Background

In 1978 Susan Easton Black stated, *"Even statistically, he [Christ] is the dominant figure of the Book of Mormon."*

With our “string” skills we are going to check her results and build an improved statistic using number of words between references.

## Pre

1. Get the scripture text and savior name data into R. This is the exact same same scripture and Savior name data as the previous "Distance Between Savior Names" task.
2. Our ultimate goal will be to display the distribution of the distance between savior names for each book in the Book of Mormon (i.e. 15 differen distributions). Ideally the plot should facilitate easy comparison between the distributions.
    - This is very similar to what we did in Part 1 task, except that there is a distribution for each book (15 total distributions).
3. On paper, make a sketch (or two) of a visualization you think would effectively show these distributions. Remember, the goal is to let your ideas dictate the tools you use, don't let your current ability or constraints of the tools you have limit you at this point. If we limited our imagination to only create visualizations that existing tools could create we would never create anything new!
    - You will have to use notional data, but the idea is to think about how variables will be mapped to aesthetics. This could be a good opportunity to learn about some new geoms!
    - Make a sketch of the dataframe(s) that would be needed to create the visualization you have envisioned. Things like variable names, data types, and example values would be goot to specify.
4. Come prepared to share you sketch with the group.

## Post

1. Use the list of Savior names and the Book of Mormon text to find the distribution of words between references to the Savior for each book in the Book of Mormon.
    * Find each instance of a Savior name in the Book of Mormon.
    * Split on those instances and then count the number of words between each instance.
    * By nesting the data you can use the `purrr` package to do this efficiently while still keeping track of the book it belongs to - which is needed for the visualizations requested below.
2. Create a plot that visualizes the distribution of words between references to the Savior for each book in the Book of Mormon. If you did the *pre class* portion of the task well, you should simply be recreating the chart sketch.
4. Create an `.Rmd`  file with one to two paragraphs summarizing your graphic that shows how the distance between Savior names is distributed across the Book of Mormon.
5. Knit and push the `.Rmd`, `.md`, and `.html` file to the GitHub repository.

### Submit

In I-learn submit a link to the `.md` file on GitHub.
:::
